newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar off lows in Tokyo, awaits U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar off lows in Tokyo, awaits U.S. jobs data.

text.p: The dollar retraced from earlier lows on short-covering by interbank traders by late Tokyo trade, as the market focused on U.S. jobs data due at 1230 GMT.

Earlier, the greenback edged down on concerns over Japan's trade surplus with the United States after a Japanese newspaper reported that the Denver summit later this month will take up the question of Japan's trade surplus, dealers said.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a Japanese business daily, quoted sources close to scheduled summit participants as saying that an economic declaration to be issued by the Group of Seven (G7) at its June 20-22 Denver summit will call on Japan to prevent its trade surplus from growing.
"The dollar was sold (for yen) in reaction to the report, which specifically mentioned Japan and the issue of preventing a rise in its trade surplus," a dealer at a trust bank said.
Despite a flurry of dollar sales following the report in the afternoon, the greenback soon pared its losses on short-covering, dealers said.

The trust bank dealer said some investment trust firms were eager to pick up dollars in connection with fresh overseas investments. Importers were also said to be placing sporadic bids, keeping the dollar supported on the downside near 115.50 yen, dealers said.

In addition, there was speculation that Japanese investors will buy dollars in order to invest some of the proceeds from the redemption of Japanese government bonds in foreign bonds and stocks, dealers said.
About five trillion yen worth of JGBs will mature on June 20.

On the upside, Japanese exporter offers checked the dollar's gains near 116 yen. Dealers said some exporters started lowering their offers after the greenback failed to break above 116.50 yen in the past few days.
"There are some offers from exporters on the upside who had failed to sell enough dollars," the trust bank dealer said.

A Japanese bank dealer in Singapore added: "Japanese investors bought dollar/yen this morning, but I think it looks heavy around 116 yen because mark/yen selling interest is strong." The mark remained weak versus the yen after breaking below key support at 67 yen overnight.

A city bank dealer in Tokyo said stop-loss mark sales may have been triggered near 66.75 yen. The German currency stood at about 66.85/88 yen at 0657 GMT, compared with 66.94 yen in late New York on Thursday.
The market was waiting for the release of May U.S. jobs data due out at 1230 GMT. The average forecast of Wall Street economists polled by Reuters called for a rise of 219,000 non-farm jobs.
The unemployment rate was expected to rise to 5.0 percent from a 23-year low of 4.9 percent last month, and average hourly earnings were seen rising 0.4 percent.
Singapore dealers said the dollar was likely to make slow progress ahead of the U.S. jobs data.
Dealers in Tokyo said that stronger-than-expected data could spark speculation of a rise in U.S. interest rates, which would boost the dollar.
Some traders added that, if the dollar rises above 1.7350 marks following the data and sets off stop-loss purchases, it could head toward the 1.74 mark level.
The dollar closed at 115.60/70 yen and 1.7275/80 marks in New York on Thursday.
--Yoko Nishikawa, Tokyo Treasuries Desk +81-3-3432-8584
--Singapore Newsroom +65-870-3080
